thread:
maria: AcmeCorp reporting intermittent 502s from hosted API since ~06:23 UTC. Started right after their token rotation window. Lots of customer hits failing. Any quick triage?

jonah: Can you paste a sample request/response + trace-id? Which edge region?

maria: sample curl and response headers below (trace-id 01FJY7):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (10.20.30.40) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/2
> authorization: Bearer <token>
< HTTP/2 502
< content-type: application/json
< x-edge-trace: 01FJY7
< x-upstream: keystone-auth/502
{"error":"bad gateway"}
```

maria: stack snippet from the edge proxy logs around that trace: 
```
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-07T06:23:12Z trace=01FJY7 upstream_error: upstream read error from keystone-auth: connection reset by peer
[keystone-auth] 2026-03-07T06:23:12Z warn: token-epoch-sweep: dropped keepalive: pool exhausted
```

deploy-bot: Canary config change deployed at 06:20 UTC: keystone token TTL shrink from 300s -> 60s for rotation testing.

tara: Hmm — that TTL shrink plus heavy fanout from Acme token rotate could cause a thundering keepalive churn. If auth backends start closing connections mid-stream, Envoy will surface 502s.

jonah: I ran a quick query against ingress metrics: 502 rate from region-us-east spiked x8 at 06:22-06:25, upstream error label contains "connection_reset" and upstream_name "keystone-auth". Kept-alive connection count to auth pool dropped ~90% in that window.

acme-support: Confirmed on our side: rotation completed at 06:21 and clients re-authing concurrently. We saw many short-lived tokens being issued.

jonah: Short-term mitigation: roll back TTL to 300s, restart keystone-auth pool gracefully to rewarm keepalives, and add a short circuit in edge to prefer healthy auth replicas (route stickiness). I can push a proxy patch to increase h2 idle timeout and reduce max concurrent streams per connection to limit churn.

tara: I'll roll back TTL and restart auth pool now (graceful drain). Also raising upstream connection pool size temporarily.

maria: Customer impact: about ~1200 failed requests over 3 minutes for Acme. They're on hosted inference with streaming turned on. They want status update.

jonah: Applying emergency proxy tweak to midfront (increase http2_keepalive_timeout  -> 90s, reduce max_concurrent_streams -> 50) and bias routing away from lagging replicas. Rolling in 3 regions.

deploy-bot: Emergency patch applied to midfront-us-east at 06:33 UTC (patch-id: patch-keystone-2026-03-07-1).

maria: After rollback + patch we see 502 rate back to baseline by 06:36. Customer confirms degraded window is over. :thumbsup:

tara: Follow-ups: full postmortem, add a canary gating step for TTL changes (simulate fanout on a small tenant group), add alert for auth pool keepalive drop.

jonah: Agreed. I'll own the postmortem draft and include mitigation playbook: detect token-rotation spikes, temporarily stretch TTL, and route around auth-backend flaps.

maria: Thanks team — forwarding this to Acme with timeline.

acme-support: Appreciate the quick response, please include any recommended client-side backoff patterns.

jonah: Will include recommended exponential backoff + jitter and advise pacing token refresh across client fleet. :thinking:
